tasks.short: Assess mental and physical status from the presenting symptoms and complaints.

steps.what: Open the chart before assessing these patients
Hear the presenting symptoms and complaints
Assess mental and physical status in the room

tasks.design: The booked appointment in {CALENDAR} opens that patient's chart in the {OTHER} patient record, which is what shortens the search. Hearing the presenting symptoms and complaints, and assessing mental and physical status, stay in the room with the nurse. No model assigns a status.
tasks.previous_blocker: The chart sat apart from the appointment book, and status is a judgement from what the nurse sees and hears.
tasks.enabler_now: The appointment already holds a patient identifier that can open the chart. The assessment itself needs no model.
tasks.still_hard: A missed affect, a minimised risk, or a physical sign still depends on the nurse in the room.
tasks.human_edge: Only the nurse can match what this person says and shows to a mental and physical status.
tasks.altitude: The nurse still hears every complaint and still assesses status in the room. The chart is open when they start. They gain no right to skip the examination.

reach.task: Review a status the nurse could not settle in the visit
reach.learn: Which signs were absent from the prior note
Which complaint the chart did not already hold

evidence.claim: Matching speech, affect and a physical sign to a mental and physical status stays with the clinician in the room. Model knowledge.
Storing a status is not a solely automated decision about the patient. The nurse makes the assessment.

assumptions: The search step is shorter only because the appointment identifier opens the chart. The nurse still reads the note. Hearing symptoms and assessing status are unchanged and stay at full time.

Chart fields opened: patient id, prior note date, prior status text, allergy list. Producer: the clinician who last wrote the note. If the link fails, the nurse searches by name inside this same step.
The appointment fields are patient id, date and time. Producer: the booking clerk in the calendar. This task does not recapture them.
No model scores status, risk or emotion. No camera and no room recording on this task.
unknowns: Whether this clinic's record already opens from the appointment.
Which status headings the service requires the nurse to cover.
research_questions: How often the chart is already on screen when the nurse calls the patient in.

already_counted.description: Read the opened chart and reselect when the appointment points at the wrong patient.

incremental.description: Point a visit at the right chart when two patients share a name.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A clinic that still puts the paper file on the desk, so the screen link is unused and the nurse still hears every symptom and assesses every patient in the room.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Diagnose psychiatric disorders and mental health conditions.

steps.what: Open the assessment for these mental health conditions
Read criteria for the suspected psychiatric disorders
Diagnose the psychiatric disorders and mental health conditions

tasks.design: The visit opens the assessment in the {OTHER} patient record, and the suspected name opens the criteria page in {DOCS}, which is what shortens the hunt through the manual. The nurse still reads the criteria. Diagnosing the psychiatric disorders and mental health conditions stays with the nurse. No model names the disorder.
tasks.previous_blocker: Criteria lived in a manual on a shelf, and naming the disorder is a judgement a keyword match gets wrong.
tasks.enabler_now: The suspected name can open the criteria page the guideline owner already published. The diagnosis needs no model.
tasks.still_hard: Comorbidity, a story that meets two criteria sets, and risk that is not written in the note.
tasks.human_edge: The nurse decides which disorder fits this person, including what the criteria page cannot see.

ambition.what: Whether each criterion the nurse relies on was open and read before the disorder is named, on follow-ups as well as first visits.

tasks.altitude: The nurse still names the disorder in the room. The criteria page is open beside the assessment. They gain no right to accept a model diagnosis.

reach.task: Review a disorder the nurse has named
reach.learn: Which criterion the nurse read and which they left unmet

evidence.claim: Choosing a psychiatric disorder from the person's account stays with the accountable clinician. Model knowledge.
The provider stays responsible for any generative tool, including errors written into the record. This task does not use one to name the disorder.
Naming the disorder is not a solely automated decision about the patient.

assumptions: Opening the assessment is shorter only because this visit already holds the note, so it opens with the encounter. The nurse still reads it.
Reading criteria is shorter only because the suspected disorder name opens the criteria page. The nurse still reads the criteria, which is why most of that step remains.

Criteria fields: disorder name, criterion id, criterion text, edition date. Producer: the guideline owner. If the page is missing, the nurse reads the printed manual in this same step. That reading time is inside the step.
Assessment fields used: patient id, visit date, note text. Producer: the nurse's own assessment in this encounter. This task does not score the nurse and does not infer emotion.
The named disorder is the nurse's decision. Nothing is written as a diagnosis until the documentation task confirms the note.
unknowns: Whether this service uses a national classification or an international one.
How often the criteria book is actually opened today.
research_questions: On a follow-up, does the nurse reopen the criteria or rely on the last named disorder?

already_counted.description: Read the opened assessment when the visit link is right.
Read the criteria page, or the printed manual when the page is missing.

incremental.description: Replace a criteria link when a new edition changes the criterion ids.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A familiar relapse where the nurse does not reopen the criteria and diagnoses from the interview alone.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Document histories, assessment results, diagnoses, plans, prescriptions and outcomes.

steps.what: Ask the medical and psychological histories
Enter physical assessment results and prescriptions
Draft histories, diagnoses, treatment plans and outcomes

loop.input: History sentences the nurse typed or dictated, plus result lines and prescription lines the nurse entered
loop.output: Draft sentences for histories, diagnoses, treatment plans and outcomes, each citing a history sentence, a result line or a prescription line
loop.check: Code rejects a sentence with no citation. The nurse rejects a sentence the visit did not say, and rejects a diagnosis, dose or outcome the nurse did not state.
loop.stop: Stop if there is no history and no entered line, if two drafts fail, or if the nurse rejects the draft. The nurse then writes the note at confirmation.
loop.why_not_simpler: The history and the outcome are free text. A fixed template cannot know which sentence was said.

steps.what: Flag interactions on the entered prescriptions
Confirm and document the patients' note

tasks.design: The nurse still asks the medical and psychological histories. A form in the {OTHER} patient record takes the physical assessment results and the prescription the nurse chose, a draft cites only those lines and the history sentences, and a rule check flags interactions against the current medication list. The nurse confirms the note before it is stored. The draft does not prescribe.
tasks.previous_blocker: The note was prose typed after the visit, and an interaction check meant hunting a reference chapter.
tasks.enabler_now: A draft can be limited to sentences the nurse already produced, and a maintained interaction file can flag a drug pair. The nurse still confirms.
tasks.still_hard: A dose that is clinically right but looks unusual, and a history the patient tells only in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The nurse decides what was actually said and whether the prescription still stands after a flag.

ambition.what: Whether each prescription was seen against the current medication list before the note is stored, on ordinary follow-ups as well as new plans.

tasks.altitude: The nurse still takes the history and still confirms the note and the prescription. A cited draft and the interaction flags are on screen first. They gain no right to let a draft prescribe or to store an unconfirmed note.

reach.task: Review the prescription after the nurse confirms it
reach.learn: Which interaction flag was on screen at confirmation
Which required heading was still empty when the nurse confirmed

evidence.claim: A consultation recorder drafts the note and the clinician validates it before it is written into the patient record. The vendor's minutes-saved claim has no published method and is not used as this task's saving.

In one European health system, self-estimated time per note fell from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes and median editing stayed 93 seconds, in a paper with three vendor authors. That is note-editing time in that study, not this task's interview or confirmation.
A national medicine file checks interactions, contraindications, doses and duplicates. The nurse still confirms the prescription.
The inspector tells providers they remain responsible for generative tools and names medication errors from a wrong registration. The nurse confirms the note before storage.
Under the medicines law a prescription is a recept. The text stored here is the one the named nurse confirmed, not a draft.
The patient dossier is kept for twenty years after the last change. This task does not shorten that.
Recording the consultation can capture how staff work, so works-council consent applies before a room recorder is switched on.

assumptions: Asking the history is unchanged and stays at full time. Confirmation of the note is a judgement and stays at full time.

The form is shorter only because fixed fields replace a blank prose box. Fields the nurse types: result type, value, unit; drug, dose, route, frequency. That typing is the capture and sits in the entry step.
The draft is shorter only because it starts from cited history sentences and entered lines, so the nurse edits instead of writing from a blank page.

The flag step is shorter only because the rule file shows matching drug pairs rather than the whole chapter. It is a review, not a zero-time machine step. If the current medication list is empty, the nurse types it in this step and that time stays in the step.
Current medication list fields: drug, dose, start date, status. Producer: the prescriber who last confirmed a line in this record.
Interaction rule fields: drug pair, severity, message. Producer: the medicines-information body. If the file is missing, the step shows no flags and the nurse uses the reference text they use today.
The confirmed version is the note on screen at confirmation, after the draft and the flags. A later edit voids it.

The design does not send the prescription to a pharmacy. Room recording stays off until works-council consent and a lawful basis for the patient are in place. Until then the nurse types the history points. The study minutes in the evidence are not this task's saving.
unknowns: Whether this service may record the room.
Which interaction file the pharmacy already maintains.
Whether the prescription is released from this screen or in a later prescribing step.
research_questions: What share of documentation time is the interview, and what share is typing after the patient leaves?

already_counted.description: Type assessment results and the prescription into the fixed fields.
Edit the draft and reject a sentence the visit did not say.
Read interaction flags and type current medicines when the list is empty.
Read the full note and confirm or reject it.

incremental.description: Clear a flag that does not match the medicine the patient is actually taking, and fix a draft citation that points at the wrong sentence.

approvals.approved_version: Draft note with histories, assessment results, diagnoses, treatment plans, prescriptions and outcomes, plus the interaction flags on screen

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A short follow-up where the nurse already knows the history, types a few lines, and the draft is empty because nothing new was said. The interview and the confirmation stay.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Educate patients and family members about conditions, medications and plans.

steps.what: Open vetted pages on the mental health conditions
Draft the explanation from those vetted paragraphs

loop.input: Topic from the confirmed disorder, the question the nurse typed, and paragraph id plus paragraph text from the opened page
loop.output: Explanation sentences, each citing one paragraph id
loop.check: Code rejects a sentence with no paragraph id. The nurse rejects a sentence that states a dose, a promise or a personal instruction the paragraph does not contain.
loop.stop: Stop if no page is open, if two drafts fail, or if the nurse rejects the draft. The nurse then explains from the page or from memory.
loop.why_not_simpler: The family's question is free text and the page is longer than the point they need. A keyword extract still adds advice the paragraph did not give.

steps.what: Educate patients and family members about the plan
Choose preventive measures, medications and treatment plans

tasks.design: The confirmed condition opens a vetted page in {DOCS}, which is what shortens the search, and a draft explains only by citing paragraphs from that page. The nurse rejects any sentence that adds a dose or a promise. Educating the patients and family members stays a conversation, and the nurse still chooses which preventive measures, medications and treatment plans to stress. Nothing is sent to the patient as a chat.
tasks.previous_blocker: The right page was hard to find during the visit, and a generated explanation can add advice the source never gave.
tasks.enabler_now: The condition name can open a page, and a draft can be forced to cite a paragraph. The conversation stays with the nurse.
tasks.still_hard: A family in crisis, low literacy, or a question the page does not cover.
tasks.human_edge: The nurse sees whether this family understood, and what must be said that the page does not contain.

ambition.what: Whether each explanation sentence cites a vetted paragraph before the nurse says it, on routine medication talks as well as new diagnoses.

tasks.altitude: The nurse still explains the plan in the room and still chooses what to stress. A cited draft is ready first. They gain no right to send an automated explanation to the patient.

reach.task: Ask about the medication during the visit
reach.learn: Which question the vetted page did not answer

reach.task: Hear what the family was told after the visit
reach.learn: Which sentence the nurse refused because the page did not say it

evidence.claim: A public patient site publishes guideline-based texts from professional bodies and a patient federation. An explanation can cite those texts. Personal advice stays with the clinician.
A patient-facing chatbot must disclose that it is AI. This design does not use one. The nurse speaks.
Explaining a plan to a distressed family is a conversation a page cannot finish. Model knowledge.

assumptions: Opening the page is shorter only because the confirmed condition name opens the matching page. The nurse still reads it.

The draft is shorter only because each sentence must cite a paragraph, so the nurse edits a short text instead of copying the page. Speaking to the family, and choosing what to stress, are unchanged and stay at full time.

Vetted page fields: topic code, paragraph id, paragraph text, review date. Producer: the patient-information publisher. The nurse opens the page in the first step. If no page matches, the draft is skipped and the nurse uses the leaflet they use today.
The topic code is the disorder the nurse already confirmed. This task does not invent a diagnosis. The draft is not given to the patient.
No emotion inference and no score of whether the family understood.
unknowns: Which psychiatric medicines the publisher actually covers.
Whether the service may hand the patient a printed extract of the page.
research_questions: How often the nurse looks up a page during the conversation today, rather than speaking from memory?

already_counted.description: Read the opened page before deciding whether to use the draft.
Reject a drafted sentence that adds a dose or a promise.

incremental.description: Retire a page link when the publisher's review date has passed and the paragraph no longer matches the talk.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most explanations are a medication the nurse already knows, said in the room with no page open, so the draft is unused and the conversation stays the whole visit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The nurse still assesses in the room, still names the disorder, still confirms the note and the prescription, and still explains the plan to the family. A chart link, a criteria page, a cited draft and interaction flags sit in front of those acts. The nurse gains no right to let a model diagnose, prescribe or speak to the patient.
reach: Psychiatrist: which disorder the nurse named, and which criterion they had open.
Pharmacist: which interaction flag was on screen when the prescription was confirmed.
Patient: which question the vetted page did not answer in the room.
skills_to_grow: Reject a note sentence the visit did not say.
Reject a disorder the criteria page does not support.
Reject an explanation that adds a dose or a promise the vetted paragraph does not contain.
role.ambitious_version: On an ordinary follow-up the nurse can see, before the family enters, whether the last confirmed status, the current medication list and the open criterion still agree. The nurse still decides.
